title: Research: bind actual selected BIT matrix preparation to PR #2310's control tables
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This takes the preparation/evaluator handoff in [discussion #2304](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2304). [PR #2310](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2310)'s iterative control evaluator was tested on independently prepared unit tables; this package **joins it to [PR #2234](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2234)'s actual full-ring selected producer**, changing neither, and checks that the compiled tables give the producer's generated child weights.

- **Adapter:** before building a table it checks the selected request, the exact frozen-field specification and that the descent is one of the actual low-class children PR #2234's `residual_plan` emits. It keeps original global slots after unit resets, and for a fallback (pair) child it uses all 128 entries of the full unweighted elimination's terminal diagonal with the final original-row permutation and the physical atom reversal: `child(i) = d_j b(pi(j), t) / b(j, t)`, with `t = i` or `f-1-i`.
- **Lemma (`PROOF.md`):** `compile_chain` followed by the unmodified PR #2310 `evaluate` returns the same unit weight as PR #2234's generated expression for every valid final atom index, on every admitted finite Good/Pair/unit-reset chain, under the stated producer normal-form hypotheses. It reads only coefficient tables at their live global slots, never the current fresh matrix or unused stock, and restores the table head. Numerical high fields at and before the last reset need not be prepared.
- **Finding:** no mismatch between the correctly bound predecessors. Three binding requirements are necessary, each shown by a concrete modulo-9 failure: full-ring rather than low-only coefficients (8 versus 2), the final original-row permutation (8 versus 1) and the physical atom reversal (2 versus 8).
- **Status:** an author-checked conditional structural proof with a finite certificate. No child-count, moment or exponent change; no supplier or κ change.

**Remaining obligations.** The producer normal forms are hypotheses here, not proved. There is no exhaustive GL64 or high-lift census, no complete payload dispatcher or selected payload execution, no physical work, parking or cleanup implementation, no instantiation of PR #2310's runtime bound, no supplier cold replay, no formalization and no independent human review.

## Task and overlap

- **Task ID / scope key:** `uniform-transfer-audit` (`603f341b99f590f17a76`), refined to `selected-BIT/PR2234-full-ring-to-PR2310-table/actual-label-mixed-reset-binding`. Chooser nonce `1666912cb72ea23ea7840a7d03438b89`, track adversarial-audit, priority revision 4; the card was the chooser's third suggestion, taken for #2304's live, named handoff (passing over `selected-stock-envelope`, whose arithmetic and rank-42 descriptor cases are covered, and the less concrete `supplier-boundary-audit`). No reroll.
- **Base and exact heads:** base `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, rechecked unchanged at 05:37 UTC; contribution `0ee2ca645f3b04e1e4df1e1055b6f9aab09eaa95`. PR #2234 `d047ef86fbc5b1614d3d8e2b8d3441413beab73f` and PR #2310 `a5258f548bfb6da71c3b72733fbbd2fb4995c929`, both Jose Manuel's and both unchanged at submission. Their consumed files are copied byte for byte under `sources/` with their notices; I checked all twelve against the two PR heads by Git blob. Main inputs are pinned in `SOURCES.json`.
- **Scope status:** refined: sampled unit tables are replaced by the actual producer's output, and the earlier descriptor identities are hypotheses, not new work.
- **Nearest work:** PR #2310 owns the control grammar and uniform-control argument, PR #2234 the producer and recursive closure; this checks the connection between them. This account's PRs #2160 and #2188 supply the earlier normal form and mixed descriptor. Gareth Davidson's PRs #2289 and #2295 formalize the recurrence and moment premises. Jose Manuel's [discussion #2319](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319), opened a minute after this claim, covers joined physical dispatch with completed children on a generic two-dimensional caller; this package is limited to coefficient binding on the actual selected requests and leaves dispatch there.
- **Claim and final check:** the claim is in [discussion #2304](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2304#discussioncomment-18941098). A final overlap check of open PRs and Discussions (complete pagination), plus a live check of newer PRs, found no other competing work.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-control-table-binding --check-only
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-control-table-binding
python3 -I -B research/selected-control-table-binding/verify.py
```

Linux x86_64, CPython 3.12.3, standard library. The registered replay (normal and optimized, plus three artifact-integrity test groups) was run again on the final package bytes before submission, under an 8 GiB memory cap: it passed in about 3 minutes and left the worktree unchanged.

```text
PASS_SELECTED_CONTROL_TABLE_BINDING fixtures=87 coordinate_equalities=801 independent_equalities=12642 controls=13
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/selected-control-table-binding outcome=completed
```

- Twelve actual selected MOVE/COPY/IDLE representatives cover every paid rank 1-7 and 42. Eighty-seven fixtures over Z/9, Z/25 and Z/27, including mixed paths with resets and nonconstant parents and a width-one root, give 801 generated-weight comparisons. An independently written normalized-elimination oracle, which builds the raw-label projector without the producer's split basis, gives 12,642 local equalities across 39 dense cases. Catalogue decoding and incoming parent descriptors are reused and credited.
- Thirteen controls reject compacted reset slots, swapped field specifications, capture of the current fresh matrix, a wrong same-rank request, an orientation or reset absent from the macroplan, a pair event on a good class, access to unused stock and a nonunit good pivot, besides the three modulo-9 failures above. A dead high-field change leaves tables and values unchanged.
- The integrity tests reject corrupted sources or blobs and altered typed receipts before import. The fixtures are an explicit bounded family, not an exhaustive census, and no large payload is executed.

- Gareth Davidson (@bitplane, PRs #2289 and #2295): the recurrence and moment formalizations behind the physical-charge handoff. The source527 and selected supplier lineage retained in `NOTICE.md`.

New work is Apache-2.0; retained notices are unchanged.

**AI assistance:** submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) did the derivation, the implementation, the checking and the writing; it was packaged and submitted with Claude Code. No independent human review is claimed.

## Open next questions

See the package README and `TASK.json`. The smallest useful follow-up, best done with #2319: connect this bound evaluator to one complete controlled-stream coefficient-preparation site, with the actual high-header spectators, inverse cleanup and local work lifetime. A separate formalization could prove the reset and extent induction on the explicit grammar.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

- **What helped:** #2304 named the missing connection precisely.
- **Friction:** the producer and the evaluator represent field age after a reset differently, which took most of the binding work.
- **Suggestion:** a compiler handoff could link the exact producer function and consumer schema and state the reset-slot invariant.
